answer: Each identity must anchor one separate stake to its own key before it may answer: the stake is locked for the whole epoch and returns only if the answer survives peer grading. One deposit cannot back two identities, so an attacker cannot grow a lotus bed of fake accounts from a single pool of coins. Climbing toward the zenith — hundreds of voting identities — then demands fresh locked capital for each one, plus forfeiture whenever duplicates are caught, so Sybil cost rises with every fake identity instead of being shared.
